name: movement disorders overview
title: Tremor or slowness: a symmetric postural or action tremor that improves with alcohol is essential tremor; asymmetric rest tremor with rigidity, bradykinesia and postural instability is parkinsonism, which is Parkinson's disease only once drugs, basal ganglia lesions, head trauma, toxins, PSP and MSA are excluded; each with its treatment and the lecture's video cases

nodes.title: Tremor or slowness: WHEN is the tremor worst, and is it on ONE side?
lines: • hyperkinetic (too much movement): ballismus · chorea · athetosis · tremor · dystonia · tics
• hypokinetic (too little): parkinsonism, with bradykinesia (slow) and akinesia (hard to start)
• rest + ASYMMETRIC + slow + small writing → parkinsonism · posture or action + SYMMETRIC + large writing → essential tremor
• parkinsonism needs NO treatment until symptoms limit function

nodes.title: Tremor with POSTURE or ACTION
lines: SYMMETRIC

nodes.title: PARKINSONISM: a syndrome
lines: tremor · rigidity · bradykinesia · postural instability, in any mix

nodes.title: Essential tremor
lines: may be hereditary · worsens over time

nodes.title: Parkinson's disease
lines: dopamine neurons of the substantia nigra die
1% of people over 60 · onset about 60
mostly sporadic, rarely hereditary

nodes.title: Parkinsonism from ANOTHER cause
lines: Parkinson's disease is only ONE cause

nodes.title: Postural or action tremor
lines: • both sides alike
• arms most, also head and voice
• improves with ALCOHOL
• LARGE, shaky handwriting (PD: micrographia)

nodes.title: case: 62, shaky hands 5+ years
lines: now spills food and drink · no other illness → reassure: NOT Parkinson's · beta-blocker after discussing side effects

nodes.title: T.R.A.P., ASYMMETRIC
lines: • Tremor at REST early, pill-rolling, hands or feet
• Rigidity: same at any speed (spasticity is velocity dependent), ↑ with augmentation
• Akinesia: rising from a chair, starting to walk
• Bradykinesia: finger or foot tapping, fist open-close, turning a doorknob
• Postural instability

nodes.title: Top to bottom
lines: • less blinking · masked face · soft, mumbling voice
• rigid, NOT spastic tone · small handwriting
• less arm swing · stooped, turns en bloc

nodes.title: Video cases
lines: • 74, no medications, told 'maybe PD' → agree, start LEVODOPA
• 60, 1 year subtle left tremor, slowness, mild rigidity → early PD, NO treatment yet
• 10 years of PD, gait worsens → medication WORE OFF

nodes.title: Ask about
lines: • antipsychotics, antiemetics (prochlorperazine, metoclopramide)
• basal ganglia stroke, bleed, tumour, infection
• repeated head trauma · carbon monoxide, cyanide

nodes.title: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP)
lines: • VERTICAL gaze palsy: pursuit and saccades overcome by vestibular reflexes
• EARLY falls, poor balance
• axial tone > limb tone · parkinsonism

nodes.title: Multiple system atrophy (MSA)
lines: • AUTONOMIC dysfunction
• + parkinsonism (MSA-P) OR cerebellar signs (MSA-C)

nodes.title: Beta-blocker or primidone
lines: other anticonvulsants are options

nodes.title: Refractory → deep brain stimulation
lines: targets in the basal ganglia

nodes.title: Not functionally limiting → no treatment yet
Limiting → LEVODOPA + carbidopa
lines: • dopamine cannot cross the blood-brain barrier; levodopa CAN
• with a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor: carbidopa (Sinemet) or benserazide (Prolopa)
• most effective: bradykinesia, rigidity best · tremor variable
• start low, titrate slowly · NEVER stop suddenly (sudden worsening)
• watch: on-off, wearing off · dyskinesia, chorea or dystonia (50% by 5 years)

nodes.title: Other options
lines: • early: MAO-B inhibitor (less dopamine breakdown)
• dopamine agonist (pramipexole, ropinirole)
• tremor: anticholinergic
• severe: deep brain stimulation
~ no proven neuroprotective drug

nodes.title: Prognosis
lines: slowly worsens · dyskinesia · depression · dementia · death usually from ASPIRATION pneumonia

nodes.title: Do NOT call it Parkinson's disease
lines: • other neurodegenerative causes: MSA, PSP, diffuse Lewy body disease
• MSA: death within 6-9 years of onset
